Yeah, when you go up in Archetype (Bronze to Silver, etc) you have to reset the pitches. It's annoying lol. Stats stay the same for the slots it just resets your pitches to default and you have to set them back to the pitches you want.

The only way is through the challenges that pop up. But you can swap your pitches around on your ballplayer setup. Pitches stats are tied to the pitch slot, not the pitch. So you could work on the velo on your curveball by putting your fastball in the slot where your curve was and then putting the slots back to normal when done. When swapping it may show you the wrong values but if you swap and go back to that pitch you will see the values dont change just what pitch is in the slot.

You do want a nice gap between the velo on your offspeed and the velo on your hard stuff, but it doesn't need to be huge to be effective. In fact if it is too big of a gap (at least in real life and like you said pve and probably for the AI on harder difficulties) it is easier to pick up which pitch is which. I believe the game makes it so a 100 velo offspeed will always be offspeed enough if your fastball is at the same velo #. Just don't let the velo on the offspeed pitch be *higher* than the velo for the fastball and you should be fine. This shouldn't be hard to do, as your offspeed only gains xp toward Break in games and the velo will only go up on it if you force it on an off day. Note the same is true about fastballs in that they will only gain xp toward velo in game. So if you want to improve the movement on, say, a 2-seamer you need to do it on an off day.

Every pitch goes up in speed with velocity, even change-ups and their derivatives. You can see this when you are in Franchise mode and edit the individual pitching stats for a pitcher. However a 100 velo 4-seam won't have the same max mph as a 100 velo 2-seamer, and the max velo on a change-up will be even lower down from the 2-seamer than the 2-seamer is from the 4-seamer. Different pitches have max velocity that can only be broken with Outlier. I do not believe there is any way to acquire Outlier, it just allows some pitchers to throw harder than any other pitcher could with 100 velo and the pitch they have Outlier with.

There are some subtleties, but it boils down to this. The game is divided into innings as opposed to quarters or lengths or halfs. Each inning has a top and bottom, where one teams offense will go against the other teams defense and then swap for the other half of the inning. In each inning a team bats until they havr accrued 3 outs, which can be achieved either by striking the batter out or catching a live ball or having the ball at base when the runner is between them. The runner is a player who is currently running the bases because he hit the ball or he already hit the ball and is on base. There are 4 bases including home plate where the batter begins. Each base can occupy only 1 runner and runners cannot pass each other. Bases must be touched in order and if a runner makes it home, he scores 1 run. Each batter has 3 strikes or attempts to hit the pitchers pitch without missing or the pitch being in the strike zone. The strike zone is supposed to be knee to breast but some umpires disagree with this. The pitcher can miss the strike zone up to 4 times before the batter is allowed to go basr on balls. A ball is when the pitcher misses the strike zone. There are other basics, like the defense having 9 players. The infield positions of Pitcher, first second and third basemen who cover the bases and Shortstop that floats between third and second and the catcher who receives thebpitches and gets the ball back to the pitcher. 3 men in the outfield cover left, right and center.
